papers.title: Cross-species molecular stratification enables T cell receptor diagnosis of Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Developing peripheral blood-based diagnostic models for idiopathic Parkinson's disease (iPD), particularly those leveraging the T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, has long been considered infeasible because patient-derived TCRs appear to lack convergent sequence motifs. We reasoned that this apparent absence of shared TCR features likely reflects both insufficient sample sizes and unaccounted immune heterogeneity within the iPD population.
papers.summary: The authors propose that the failure to find shared T-cell receptor motifs in Parkinson's disease blood samples stems from small sample sizes and hidden immune heterogeneity among patients. They introduce a cross-species molecular stratification approach to subgroup patients, enabling TCR-based diagnostic models for idiopathic Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: Biological rationales from language models enable leakage-resistant forecasts of target-indication success.
papers.abstract: Identifying which target-indication (T-I) hypotheses can translate into clinical success remains a central challenge in drug discovery. We present PRIORITI (Prospective Rationale-Informed Outcome Reasoning for Integrated Target-indication Intelligence), a leakage-resistant framework that separates upstream biological evidence synthesis from outcome prediction. Given only a target gene and disease indication, a domain-instructed large language model (LLM) synthesizes drug-agnostic human genetics across prespecified channels. These evidence were embedded and combined with static entity context d
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce PRIORITI, a framework that uses a domain-instructed large language model to synthesize drug-agnostic human genetic evidence for a target-indication pair, then predicts clinical success from these embeddings plus static entity context. By separating evidence synthesis from outcome prediction, the approach avoids data leakage that can inflate retrospective benchmarks. The method aims to improve prospective forecasts of which target-indication hypotheses will succeed in the clinic.

papers.title: AI-Based Comparison of UniProt annotations and Literature Across Human Kinases.
papers.abstract: Curated protein records and their supporting publications organize biological evidence at different levels of detail. Here, we used AI to independently answer a set of biological questions using either UniProt records or the full texts of the literature cited by those records, and then used AI-based evaluation to compare the resulting answers in terms of information coverage and semantic agreement. Fifty human proteins were selected from ten groups in a kinase sequence collection. Target-identity filtering retained 1,749 protein-publication records representing 1,655 distinct publications. For
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses AI to compare the information content of UniProt protein records against the full text of the publications they cite, focusing on 50 human kinases. The authors find that UniProt annotations and the underlying literature provide different levels of detail and coverage, with AI-based evaluation revealing gaps and semantic differences between curated records and their supporting publications.

papers.title: KRstereo: Predicting β-Hydroxy Stereochemistry in Polyketides Using Protein Language Models.
papers.abstract: Polyketides are a major class of bioactive natural products whose activities are often determined by the stereochemistry of β-hydroxyl groups. In type I polyketide synthases (PKSs), ketoreductase (KR) domains establish these stereocenters, making accurate prediction of KR stereochemistry important for natural product discovery and PKS engineering. Existing rule-based methods rely on a limited set of sequence motifs and often perform poorly across phylogenetically diverse taxa. Here, we present KRstereo, a machine learning framework that predicts KR stereochemistry directly from sequence. Analy
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: KRstereo is a machine learning framework that predicts the stereochemistry of β-hydroxyl groups in polyketides by analyzing ketoreductase (KR) domain sequences using protein language models. It outperforms existing rule-based methods that rely on limited sequence motifs, especially across phylogenetically diverse taxa. This enables better prediction of natural product stereochemistry and supports PKS engineering.

papers.title: Nutrient Calculation Accuracy, Expert-Rated Clinical Appropriateness and Safety Indicators, and Reproducibility of Large Language Model-Generated Diet Plans for Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome: A Real-Case-Based Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the nutrient calculation accuracy, reproducibility, and expert-rated clinical appropriateness and safety indicators of three-day diet plans generated for women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), recently proposed to be termed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Methods: Anonymized data from six women with heterogeneous PMOS profiles, purposively selected from a single clinic, were converted into standardized Turkish prompts and submitted to ChatGPT-4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Mistral 2.0 through free web interfaces. T
papers.summary: This study evaluated four large language models (ChatGPT-4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Mistral 2.0) for generating three-day diet plans for women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS/PMOS). Using real anonymized patient cases, the authors assessed nutrient calculation accuracy, reproducibility across repeated runs, and expert-rated clinical appropriateness and safety. The work provides a real-case-based benchmark of LLM reliability for clinical nutrition planning in a specific patient population.

papers.title: [pMHCBind: predicting major histocompatibility complex class I-peptide interactions via protein large language models and hypergraph neural networks].
papers.abstract: Major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC I) molecules initiate CD8+ T cell immune responses by presenting antigenic peptides, a process fundamentally governed by the spatial interaction network mediated by multi-residue synergy between the binding groove and the peptide. Accurate modeling of this mechanism is crucial for tumor neoantigen screening and personalized immunotherapy. However, existing methods are largely confined to sequence-level modeling, failing to capture cross-residue higher-order structural dependencies and fine-grained binding interface interactions. To address these ch
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: The paper introduces pMHCBind, a computational method that predicts whether antigenic peptides will bind to MHC class I molecules by combining protein large language models with hypergraph neural networks. This approach aims to capture higher-order structural dependencies between residues that sequence-only methods miss, which could improve tumor neoantigen screening and personalized immunotherapy design.

papers.title: Large language models poorly capture how word order shapes representations of sentence meaning in the human brain.
papers.abstract: Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. Using representational similarity analysis, we compared representations from eight transformers and eleven other
papers.summary: This study used 7T fMRI to compare how transformer language models and the human brain represent sentence meaning when word order is manipulated independently of word meaning. The authors found that transformer representations poorly capture how word order shapes neural representations of sentence meaning, suggesting LLMs do not process syntax-meaning interactions in a human-like way.

papers.title: Multiomic characterization of microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer reveals distinct biology and targetable vulnerabilities.
papers.abstract: Microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC) is a molecularly complex and clinically challenging disease subtype, lacking effective targeted therapies. Leveraging multiomic data from ∼2,000 tumor samples (including 316MSS CRCs not previously profiled) representing ∼4,500 molecular profiles and 195,246 single cells/nuclei, we uncover complex biology and therapeutic vulnerabilities. Application of a multiomic-phenomic integrative framework, including iPhenMap (a machine-learning tool), reveals complex molecular programs, including replication stress, right-sided biology, glutaminolysis-dr
papers.summary: This study presents a large multiomic characterization of microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer, integrating data from ~2,000 tumor samples, ~4,500 molecular profiles, and ~195,000 single cells/nuclei to uncover distinct molecular programs. Using a machine-learning framework called iPhenMap, the authors identify biological features such as replication stress, right-sided tumor biology, and glutaminolysis-driven programs, along with targetable vulnerabilities. The work provides a comprehensive resource for understanding this clinically challenging CRC subtype and nominates potential therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Ex vivo JAK and TNF inhibitor-modulated immune signatures guide first-line therapy selection in rheumatoid arthritis.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a heterogeneous autoimmune disease for which selecting the most appropriate first targeted therapy remains challenging. We integrated ex vivo immune-cell functional assays, targeted proteomics, clinical outcomes, and a three-dimensional (3D) synovial model to identify treatment-associated molecular signatures and evaluate their relationship with subsequent response to Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) or tumour necrosis factor inhibitors (TNFi).
papers.summary: This study integrates ex vivo immune-cell functional assays, targeted proteomics, clinical outcomes, and a 3D synovial model to identify molecular signatures associated with response to JAK inhibitors versus TNF inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis. The goal is to guide first-line targeted therapy selection in a heterogeneous disease where such choices are currently difficult.

papers.title: DNA Fragment Length Analysis Using Machine Learning Assisted Vibrational Spectroscopy.
papers.abstract: DNA length analysis is essential for genomic workflows including next-generation sequencing and fragmentomics-based diagnostics. Conventional approaches typically require large, expensive instrumentation and sample-destructive protocols with long processing times. Here we present a rapid, label-free approach integrating vibrational spectroscopy with deep learning to quantify DNA fragment length distributions. We demonstrate that ATR-FTIR and Raman spectroscopy capture length-dependent spectral features arising from phosphate backbone, nucleobase, and structural vibrations. Machine learning mod
papers.summary: This paper presents a label-free method for analyzing DNA fragment length distributions by combining vibrational spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR and Raman) with deep learning. The approach captures length-dependent spectral features from phosphate backbone, nucleobase, and structural vibrations, offering a rapid alternative to conventional size-separation methods. It has potential applications in genomic workflows such as next-generation sequencing and fragmentomics-based diagnostics.

papers.title: HRDPath: an explainable multi-model deep learning architecture for predicting homologous recombination deficiency from histopathology images.
papers.abstract: Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is a critical biomarker for guiding treatment decisions in high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC), a cancer with few reliable biomarkers. However, existing genomics-based tests for HRD are variable, expensive, and time-consuming. We develop HRDPath, a patient-level deep learning architecture that predicts HRD status from whole slide images, requiring no additional molecular testing. HRDPath is validated across three cohorts of female patients and achieves an AUC of 0.846, significantly outperforming previously reported results in HGSOC. By in
papers.summary: HRDPath is a deep learning model that predicts homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) status directly from routine histopathology whole-slide images of high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma, avoiding the need for costly and variable genomic tests. Validated across three patient cohorts, it achieved an AUC of 0.846, outperforming prior HGSOC results, and is designed to be explainable via a multi-model architecture.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Amyloidogenic Polypeptide Research: From Sequence Prediction to Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, machine learning (ML) has established a transformative paradigm for investigating amyloidogenic polypeptides. Characterized by their propensity to form ordered, β-sheet-rich fibrillar aggregates, these polypeptides are centrally implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). This review systematically evaluates the application of ML across critical domains of amyloid investigation: sequence-based amyloidogenicity prediction, structural biology, inhibitor design, and amyloid-related cl
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning is being applied across amyloid research, from predicting amyloidogenic sequences to structural biology and inhibitor/drug design for diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's. It organizes the field into key application domains and evaluates the methods used in each.

papers.title: Protein-Protein Interface Residue Prediction by Integrating Protein Language Representations and Structural Graph Attention.
papers.abstract: Accurate residue-level prediction of protein-protein interaction interfaces is important for elucidating molecular recognition mechanisms and guiding targeted drug design. However, interface residues are relatively sparse and governed by complex spatial dependencies, making their accurate identification challenging. In this study, we developed EvoStruct-GAT, a multimodal graph attention model based on the PDBbind v2020.R1 data set. To reduce information leakage arising from sequence homology, receptor and ligand sequences were clustered independently, and the resulting clusters were used to co
papers.summary: The authors present EvoStruct-GAT, a multimodal graph attention model that combines protein language model representations with structural graph features to predict which residues lie at protein-protein interfaces. They build the model on PDBbind v2020.R1 and mitigate sequence-homology leakage by clustering receptor and ligand sequences independently before splitting data. The approach targets the sparse, spatially complex nature of interface residues to improve residue-level prediction for drug design applications.

papers.title: VAE-based synthetic volume generation for trabecular bone microarchitecture.
papers.abstract: Micro computed tomography (microCT) enables detailed characterization of trabecular bone microarchitecture through quantitative morphological parameters. However, trabecular bone exhibits morphological variability across species, anatomical locations, bone types, and physiological or pathological conditions. Individual microCT datasets generally represent only a limited portion of this morphological variability, which may constrain the development and validation of quantitative descriptors, image-processing pipelines, and computational models. This study presents a Variational Autoencoder (VAE
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: This paper introduces a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) framework to generate synthetic microCT volumes of trabecular bone, aiming to capture the morphological variability that individual datasets lack. By producing realistic synthetic bone microarchitecture, the method could support the development and validation of quantitative descriptors, image-processing pipelines, and computational models. The approach addresses the limited morphological diversity in single microCT datasets across species, anatomical sites, and disease states.

papers.title: PAZy: an expanded and actively maintained database of experimentally validated plastic-active enzymes.
papers.abstract: The Plastics-Active Enzyme Database (PAZy) is a manually curated resource for enzymes experimentally shown to act on synthetic or bio-based plastics. It was developed to distinguish experimentally verified plastics-active enzymes from computationally predicted or insufficiently supported candidates. Here, we present an expanded version of PAZy, implemented as a relational database containing >450 plastics-active enzymes with more detailed metadata, broader substrate coverage, and large language model-assisted curation of activity data. The redesigned web interface now enables browsing by prote
papers.summary: PAZy is a manually curated database of over 450 experimentally validated plastic-active enzymes, now expanded with richer metadata, broader substrate coverage, and LLM-assisted curation of activity data. It distinguishes verified plastic-degrading enzymes from merely predicted candidates, and offers a redesigned web interface for browsing by protein, substrate, and other criteria. This resource supports research on plastic biodegradation and enzyme engineering.

papers.title: DeepNPA: A protBert-based framework for residue-level annotation of neuropeptide precursors.
papers.abstract: Neuropeptides are key signaling molecules that regulate the nervous and endocrine systems, and their maturation depends on precise proteolytic cleavage of precursor proteins. However, residue-level annotation remains essential yet experimentally labor intensive, with limited dedicated computational tools. Here, we present DeepNPA, a residue-level annotation framework that integrates ProtBert, a pretrained protein language model, with focal loss for imbalance-aware optimization. DeepNPA was trained and evaluated on a non-redundant Swiss-Prot-derived dataset annotated using the BIO scheme. On a
papers.summary: DeepNPA is a computational framework that uses ProtBert, a pretrained protein language model, combined with focal loss to annotate neuropeptide precursor proteins at the residue level. It was trained on a non-redundant Swiss-Prot-derived dataset using the BIO labeling scheme, aiming to replace labor-intensive experimental annotation of cleavage sites and mature peptides.

papers.title: Multimodal Hyperspectral Imaging Unveils Pigment Rearrangement in the Diatom Cyclotella meneghiniana under Changing Physicochemical Conditions.
papers.abstract: Revealing the spatial organization and stress-induced rearrangements of the photosynthetic machinery in thylakoids of diatoms is crucial for understanding their metabolic responses and/or adaptation. Using a multimodal framework that combines coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS), two-photon excited fluorescence, and confocal fluorescence microscopy with machine learning, we investigated the spatial pigment distribution in thylakoids of Cyclotella meneghiniana. Under physiological conditions, we observed dense central packing of fucoxanthins (Fx's). In contrast, the peripheral girdle la
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters
papers.summary: This study uses a multimodal imaging platform combining coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering, two-photon excited fluorescence, and confocal fluorescence microscopy with machine learning to map pigment distribution in diatom thylakoids. Under normal conditions, fucoxanthin pigments are densely packed in the center of the thylakoid, but under changing physicochemical conditions they rearrange toward the periphery. The work reveals stress-induced spatial reorganization of photosynthetic pigments that likely reflects metabolic adaptation in diatoms.

papers.title: Beyond prediction: The evolving role of artificial intelligence in genome editing.
papers.abstract: Since the discovery of the clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat (CRISPR)-associated (Cas) system, genome-editing technologies have advanced rapidly, and the field has expanded substantially. In parallel, artificial intelligence (AI) has progressed at an unprecedented pace and is transforming genetic engineering. Early AI applications primarily addressed predictive tasks, including guide RNA (gRNA) activity, off-target effects, and editing outcomes for CRISPR-Cas nucleases, base editors, and prime editors. Recently, transformer-based protein language models (PLMs) and genera
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence is moving beyond simple prediction tasks in CRISPR genome editing, such as forecasting guide RNA activity and off-target effects, toward more ambitious applications. It highlights recent advances in transformer-based protein language models and generative AI that are beginning to design and engineer editing components themselves, transforming genetic engineering from prediction to creation.

papers.title: CLEAN Database: providing enzyme function coverage for over 55 million sequences.
papers.abstract: Enzyme function annotation is critical for decoding biological systems and enabling rational enzyme design. However, experimentally characterized enzyme functions remain available for only a small fraction of known protein sequences, resulting in a widening gap between rapidly expanding sequence space and reliable functional assignments. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have accelerated enzyme function annotation by facilitating accurate and high-throughput prediction from protein sequences. Here, we present CLEAN Database (CLEAN DB), a comprehensive resource encompassing >55 mi
papers.summary: CLEAN DB is a new database that provides predicted enzyme function annotations for over 55 million protein sequences, addressing the gap between the vast number of known sequences and the small fraction with experimentally characterized functions. It leverages AI-based prediction methods to assign enzyme functions at high throughput, offering broad coverage of sequence space for researchers studying enzymes and designing new ones.

papers.title: scChronos: Hierarchical Temporal Context Learning for Missing Snapshot Prediction in Single-Cell Time Series.
papers.abstract: Single-cell time-series atlases provide discrete cross-sectional snapshots of continuous developmental processes, making missing-snapshot prediction essential for reconstructing trajectories and dynamic programs. However, destructive scRNA-seq profiling prevents tracking the same cells across time, yielding unpaired population snapshots and making missing-snapshot prediction challenging. Existing methods typically rely on explicit dynamical propagation or transport-based coupling between snapshots, which may ignore the statistical constraints of the overall population distribution and be sensi
papers.summary: scChronos introduces a hierarchical temporal context learning framework to predict missing snapshots in single-cell time-series data, addressing the challenge of unpaired population snapshots caused by destructive scRNA-seq profiling. Unlike existing methods that rely on explicit dynamical propagation or transport-based coupling, it leverages statistical constraints of the overall population distribution to improve robustness. This enables more accurate reconstruction of continuous developmental trajectories from discrete cross-sectional atlases.

papers.title: Quantifying pollen and spore morphology using a language model.
papers.abstract: In a typical systematic paper, specimen morphology is described with natural language, and taxonomic specialists use glossaries of technical terminology to establish and communicate taxon concepts, using morphology to delimit species. Textual descriptions of specimen morphology are therefore foundational to biological systematics, but they also serve as a primary data source for studies of morphological evolution. Typically, researchers extract attributes of taxon morphology from descriptions and analyse them to quantify how organismal form has evolved. Focussing on fossil pollen and spores as
papers.summary: This paper applies a language model to extract morphological descriptions of fossil pollen and spores from systematic literature, enabling quantitative analysis of specimen form. It demonstrates how natural-language taxonomic descriptions can be converted into structured data for studying morphological evolution. The approach offers a scalable way to mine legacy biodiversity text for morphological traits.

papers.title: AGENTi: APCI-ESI Analyte Ionization Fidelity Pre-Screening Workflow using Multimodel Inference.
papers.abstract: Ionization sources convert neutral analytes into ions, enabling their subsequent separation and detection by mass spectrometry. Depending on the technique, this mechanism occurs within a solution or in the gas phase. The two most common methods to generate ions are electrospray ionization (ESI) and atmospheric-pressure chemical ionization (APCI), respectively. Both ESI and APCI can generate the same resultant ion species; however, it has been shown that preferential charge sites can change in response to an ionization source environment. Therefore, an additional quality control is warranted a
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: AGENTi is a computational workflow that predicts whether a given analyte will ionize preferentially via ESI or APCI before running mass spectrometry experiments. It uses multimodel inference to integrate predictions from multiple models, providing a pre-screening quality-control step that can guide ionization source selection and reduce trial-and-error in method development.

papers.title: Assessing the Generalizability of Machine Learning and Physics-Based Methods with DNA-Encoded Libraries.
papers.abstract: Predicting protein-ligand binding is a central challenge in computational drug discovery, and while machine learning (ML) and cofolding methods have advanced rapidly, their ability to generalize beyond training or parametrization regimes remains insufficiently understood. DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) enable ultralarge screening of billions of molecules simultaneously, providing a useful testbed for evaluating these approaches at scale. A recent NeurIPS competition revealed that even top-performing ML models trained on DEL data failed at generalizing to out-of-distribution (OOD) chemical space.
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This paper evaluates how well machine learning and physics-based protein-ligand binding prediction methods generalize when tested on DNA-encoded library (DEL) data, which enables screening of billions of molecules. Building on a NeurIPS competition, the authors show that even top ML models trained on DEL data fail to generalize to out-of-distribution chemical space, highlighting a key limitation for computational drug discovery.

papers.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence to Unveil Patterns of Antioxidant Peptides for Free Radical Regulation.
papers.abstract: Antioxidant peptides are emerging as promising therapeutic and nutraceutical agents because of their capacity to neutralize free radicals, modulate oxidative stress, and contribute to disease prevention in fields ranging from oncology to dermatology and food science. However, traditional computational approaches often fail to capture the biochemical semantics and evolutionary context of peptide sequences, limiting the predictive accuracy and mechanistic interpretability. Here, we present an explainable deep learning framework integrating evolutionary scale modeling (ESM) embeddings with a temp
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors present an explainable deep learning framework that combines ESM protein language model embeddings with a temporal/sequence model to predict antioxidant peptide activity against free radicals. The explainability component reveals sequence and biochemical patterns associated with antioxidant function, improving both predictive accuracy and mechanistic interpretability over traditional computational approaches.

papers.title: Development and Preclinical Evaluation of Novel STK3/4 Inhibitors with Anti-Obesity Potential.
papers.abstract: Obesity is associated with impaired adipocyte metabolism driven in part by mitochondrial dysfunction. Serine/threonine-protein kinase 3 (STK3) and STK4 promote mitophagy, leading to reduced mitochondrial mass in adipose tissue. Thus, inhibition of STK3/4 represents a potential therapeutic strategy for obesity and related metabolic disorders.
papers.summary: The authors developed and tested novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting STK3/4 kinases, which promote mitophagy and reduce mitochondrial mass in adipose tissue. Preclinical evaluation suggests these inhibitors may improve adipocyte metabolism and have anti-obesity potential. This work positions STK3/4 inhibition as a new therapeutic strategy for obesity and related metabolic disorders.

papers.title: A unified framework for quantitative splicing and transcript prediction.
papers.abstract: RNA splicing is frequently disrupted by genetic variation, contributing to a wide range of human diseases. Identifying the variants responsible for altered splicing is therefore crucial but has long been challenging. Deep learning models that predict splicing from genomic sequence have substantially advanced their detection, but accurately resolving their quantitative effects on splicing and the resulting transcripts remains an unmet need. Here we introduce SpliceAI2, a deep learning model trained end-to-end on splice site, splice junction, and transcript usage across multiple mammalian specie
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The paper introduces SpliceAI2, a deep learning model that predicts not only splice sites and junctions but also the quantitative effects of genetic variants on splicing and the resulting transcript usage across multiple mammalian species. This addresses a key gap in linking genetic variation to altered splicing and downstream transcript outcomes, which is important for understanding disease mechanisms.

papers.title: PrOMet: Accurate and Robust Metal-Binding Site and Type Prediction.
papers.abstract: Metal binding to proteins is crucial for many biological functions, yet the prediction of metal-binding sites and metal types remains underexplored compared to other biomolecular interactions. Despite advances in deep learning, computational methods have achieved limited success in this area; even the best-reported approaches reach only moderate localization accuracy on high-resolution crystal structures, and even worse when applied to medium-resolution data. We hypothesize that the main challenge lies in the nature of metal binding. While the putative sites span the entire protein surface, ac
papers.summary: PrOMet is a new deep learning method for predicting where metals bind on protein surfaces and which metal type binds there. The authors argue that the main difficulty is that putative binding sites cover the whole protein surface while actual sites are sparse, and their approach improves localization accuracy on both high- and medium-resolution crystal structures compared to prior methods.

papers.title: A High-Content Pseudotime Framework for Morphological Profiling of Dengue Virus Inhibitors from a Drug-Repurposing Library.
papers.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) causes dengue fever, a globally prevalent, epidemic-prone disease with no FDA-approved antivirals. Additionally, the available vaccine for DENV can increase the risk of severe dengue fever for those who have never had a DENV infection due to antibody-dependent enhancement. Thus, there is an urgent need to identify DENV antivirals. Drug repurposing, high-content screening, and machine learning were leveraged to efficiently identify antivirals likely to inhibit DENV replication. Using high-content screening in a DENV infection model, we characterized the morphological pattern
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study combines high-content morphological screening with a pseudotime framework and machine learning to profile dengue virus inhibitors from a drug-repurposing library. The approach characterizes how cellular morphology evolves during DENV infection and uses this trajectory to identify compounds likely to inhibit viral replication. It offers a scalable strategy for antiviral discovery against a disease lacking approved therapeutics.

papers.title: A transient third metal ion shapes the catalytic cycle of a group I intron ribozyme.
papers.abstract: The self-splicing group I intron ribozyme from Tetrahymena thermophillia (THr) is a prototypical example of how RNA overcomes its limited chemical repertoire to form complex, negatively charged junctions and catalyze chemical reactions. Despite over 30 years of bio-chemical and structural characterization, questions still remain regarding the requirements for THr catalysis that may inform structure based drug design against group I introns, as well as the use of THr as an RNA editing tool. Recent cryo-EM structures have provided an unprecedented window into the first and second steps of splici
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint uses cryo-EM structures to investigate how the Tetrahymena group I intron ribozyme catalyzes RNA splicing, focusing on the role of metal ions in the active site. The authors identify a transient third metal ion that appears to shape the catalytic cycle, refining the long-standing two-metal-ion mechanism for this classic ribozyme. The work has implications for structure-based drug design targeting group I introns and for engineering the ribozyme as an RNA editing tool.

papers.title: Massively Multiplexed Photonic Chip With Cross-Channel Fusion For Harmonized Biosensing.
papers.abstract: Accurate, label-free analysis of complex biological mixtures is limited by poor multiplexing scalability and inconsistent responses across sensor samples. We introduce a transformative sensing platform that integrates large-scale photonic multiplexing with data-driven analytics to overcome these constraints. Our modular, affordable glass-chip whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) photonic architecture is designed to support simultaneous readout of up to 100 sensing channels comprising over 10 000 high-Q microresonators, exceeding existing multiplexing capabilities by more than two orders of magnitude.
papers.summary: The authors present a glass-chip photonic sensing platform based on whispering-gallery-mode microresonators that can read out up to 100 sensing channels containing over 10,000 high-Q resonators simultaneously, exceeding prior multiplexing by more than two orders of magnitude. They pair this hardware with data-driven cross-channel fusion analytics to harmonize inconsistent sensor responses, enabling label-free analysis of complex biological mixtures.

papers.title: Protein Language Models Identify Early Folding Residues as Critical Hotspots for Pathogenic Variants and Cancer Prognosis.
papers.abstract: Identifying the specific residues that initiate protein folding is critical for understanding protein stability and the mechanisms of misfolding-related diseases. However, the systematic, proteome-wide identification of these early folding residues (EFRs) has been hampered by both experimental and computational limitations. Here, we present LMEFold, a deep learning framework using protein language models (PLMs) to accurately predict EFRs from amino acid sequence alone. LMEFold outperforms existing sequence-based predictors on the Start2Fold benchmark (ROC AUC = 0.831), and its predicted scores
papers.summary: The authors present LMEFold, a deep learning framework that uses protein language models to predict early folding residues (EFRs) directly from amino acid sequence, outperforming existing sequence-based predictors on the Start2Fold benchmark (ROC AUC = 0.831). They then show that predicted EFRs are enriched for pathogenic variants and are associated with cancer prognosis, suggesting these residues are critical functional hotspots.

papers.title: Predicted structure of the complete CPLANE complex reveals novel interactors and mechanisms of Jbts17 during ciliogenesis.
papers.abstract: Cilia are highly conserved organelles that use hundreds of unique proteins to drive extracellular motility and serve as signaling hubs for eukaryotic cells. The Ciliogenesis and Planar Polarity Effector (CPLANE) protein complex controls basal body docking during early ciliogenesis and recruits the intraflagellar transport (IFT) proteins to the base of growing cilia. Leveraging recent advantages in deep learning neural networks and high-performance computing, we predict the structure of JBTS17, the largest CPLANE subunit, and the tertiary structure of the complete CPLANE complex, revealing dire
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors used deep learning-based structure prediction to model JBTS17, the largest subunit of the CPLANE complex, and the complete CPLANE complex, which controls basal body docking during ciliogenesis. The predicted structures reveal novel protein interactors and suggest mechanisms by which Jbts17 functions in cilium formation. This provides structural insight into a disease-relevant complex linked to ciliopathies such as Joubert syndrome.

papers.title: Rapid Species-Level Classification of Urinary Pathogens from Raw LC-MS/MS Signals Using Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Urinary tract infections are among the most common infections in humans, yet their diagnosis still depends on time-consuming workflows based on microbial culture, followed by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry. Although LC-MS/MS offers the sensitivity and specificity needed to bypass culture, conventional pipelines depend on lengthy analyses and peptide/protein identification steps, limiting the throughput and hindering its adoption in clinical settings. Here, we introduce a direct, identification-free LC-MS/MS workflow that analyzes raw ion signal and produces species-level microbial identification
papers.summary: The authors present a machine learning workflow that classifies urinary pathogens to the species level directly from raw LC-MS/MS ion signals, bypassing conventional peptide/protein identification and culture steps. This identification-free approach could substantially shorten turnaround time and improve throughput for urinary tract infection diagnostics compared with culture-plus-MALDI-TOF workflows.

papers.title: PepRePs: Peptide-Retargeted Phosphatases Designed with Generative Language Models.
papers.abstract: Phosphorylation is a fast, reversible layer of post-translational control that directly governs protein activity, signaling flux, and cell state. Kinases and phosphatases collectively establish these phosphorylation states, but their dysregulation drives cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, and developmental disorders. Selectively manipulating the phosphorylation of individual proteins in cells remains challenging, particularly for disordered substrates. Here, we introduce Pep tide- Re targeted P hosphatase s ( PepRePs ), a genetically encoded system that fuses a peptide binder to a serine/thre
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce PepRePs, a genetically encoded system that fuses a peptide binder to a serine/threonine phosphatase, enabling selective dephosphorylation of individual target proteins in cells. Because the peptide binder can be designed with generative language models, the approach offers a programmable way to retarget phosphatase activity toward specific substrates, including disordered proteins that are otherwise hard to manipulate. This addresses a long-standing gap in the ability to control phosphorylation states with protein-level precision.

papers.title: Digital Twins in Oncology: From Multimodal Data Integration to Precision Clinical Practice.
papers.abstract: Oncology digital twins are patient-specific computational models that are built by combining electronic health records, multiomics genomic data, and diagnostic imaging to simulate individual tumor biology and predict multiple treatment-related outcomes. Conceptually originated from aerospace engineering, it has matured clinically through convergent advances in radiomics, mechanistic tumor modeling, pharmacokinetic- pharmacodynamic systems, federated machine learning, and, most recently, large language model (LLM)-based clinical interfaces and agentic artificial intelligence (AI). For a practic
papers.journal: The Indian journal of radiology & imaging
papers.summary: This review describes how oncology digital twins—patient-specific computational models built from electronic health records, multiomics data, and diagnostic imaging—can simulate individual tumor biology and predict treatment outcomes. It traces the concept from aerospace engineering to clinical maturity through advances in radiomics, mechanistic tumor modeling, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic systems, federated machine learning, and LLM-based clinical interfaces and agentic AI. The paper is aimed at practitioners, outlining the path from multimodal data integration to precision clinical practice.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Deep Learning Integrating Multi-Regional MRI and Clinical Features for Predicting Biochemical Recurrence After Radical Prostatectomy: A Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: Existing deep learning models for predicting biochemical recurrence (BCR) after radical prostatectomy often ignore the biological context beyond the tumor. This study aims to develop and validate a transformer-based model combining multi-regional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features and clinical data to improve BCR prediction after radical prostatectomy in prostate cancer (PCa).
papers.summary: This multicenter study develops a transformer-based deep learning model that combines MRI features from multiple prostate regions (not just the tumor) with clinical data to predict biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy. The approach aims to capture biological context beyond the tumor itself, potentially improving recurrence prediction over tumor-only models.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Dementia Research: Trends, Biomarkers, Prediction Goals, and Data Modalities.
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in dementia research for diagnosis, early detection, prognosis, biomarker characterization, and disease phenotyping. This study aimed to provide a bibliometric and thematic overview of ML applications in dementia, emphasizing biological mechanisms, prediction goals, data modalities, collaborative networks, and emerging computational approaches.
papers.summary: This bibliometric and thematic review maps how machine learning is being applied across dementia research, covering diagnosis, early detection, prognosis, biomarker characterization, and disease phenotyping. It catalogs the biological mechanisms targeted, prediction goals, data modalities used, and collaborative networks, while highlighting emerging computational approaches. The work provides a structured overview of trends rather than new empirical findings.

papers.title: Empathy in the Soil, Agents on the Desktop: Why Plant Pathology Needs a Scientist-in-the-Loop AI Paradigm.
papers.abstract: Plant pathology faces a cognitive bottleneck caused by the growing volume of biological data. Addressing it requires a shift from passive chatbots to autonomous AI research agents that operate in Goal-Action-State cycles. Researchers can set up a local, desktop-based agentic framework that combines semantic discovery, LLM-Wiki knowledge synthesis, and in silico prevalidation, managed under a human-directed three-tier organizational model. Strict "Scientist-in-the-Loop" boundaries, which means that a human researcher sets the goals, reviews AI-generated output before it is treated as evidence,
papers.summary: This perspective article argues that plant pathology is constrained by a cognitive bottleneck from expanding biological data, and proposes moving beyond passive chatbots to autonomous AI research agents that operate in Goal-Action-State cycles. The authors describe a local, desktop-based agentic framework integrating semantic discovery, LLM-Wiki knowledge synthesis, and in silico prevalidation, governed by a three-tier human-directed model with strict Scientist-in-the-Loop boundaries where researchers set goals and vet AI output before it counts as evidence.

papers.title: Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have largely been driven by large language models, deep neural networks that operate over discrete units called tokens. To represent text, most large language models use words or word fragments as the tokens, known as subword tokenization1. Subword tokenization obscures fine-grained information, which is problematic, especially for scientific data-such as computer code or biological sequences-where meaning depends on the individual characters or bytes2. Models that instead operate directly on the byte encoding of text avoid these limitations, but
papers.summary: The paper presents a method to retrofit existing language models so they can operate directly on raw bytes instead of subword tokens. This preserves fine-grained character-level information important for scientific data like code and biological sequences, while leveraging pretrained models.

papers.title: A machine learning classifier reveals hidden rare biallelic heterozygous variants in the coding regions of Meniere disease genome.
papers.abstract: Meniere disease (MD) is a rare inner ear disorder with a significant genetic contribution. We developed the MD classifier, an ML tool to distinguish familial from sporadic MD cases using rare variants in coding regions. We have generated a disease-specific gene variant score incorporating gene, variant, and disease-specific features. A gradient boosting classifier achieved the highest performance, with a test AUC of 0.843 (95% CI, 0.702-0.948) and an accuracy of 81.5%. Reclassification of sporadic cases into the familial group ranged from 16.6% to 28.3%. The model identified a burden of bialle
papers.summary: The authors built a machine learning classifier (gradient boosting) that uses rare coding-region variants to distinguish familial from sporadic Meniere disease cases, achieving a test AUC of 0.843 and 81.5% accuracy. Reclassifying sporadic cases as familial (16.6–28.3%) revealed a hidden burden of biallelic heterozygous variants, suggesting some apparently sporadic cases may have a genetic basis.

papers.title: DNA augmentations for semi-supervised learning in genomic sequence classification.
papers.abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) is a natural fit for genomics, where unlabeled sequences are abundant but high-quality labels are scarce due to costly curation. However, most SSL pipelines rely on generic perturbations that are not tailored to biological constraints, and it remains unclear which augmentation designs yield reliable gains for DNA sequence classification. In this application note, we present an empirical study of genome-aware weak-strong augmentation recipes for pseudo-label-based SSL, focusing on FixMatch and FlexMatch with a GROVER DNA language model backbone. Across two classif
papers.summary: This paper empirically evaluates genome-aware weak-strong augmentation strategies for semi-supervised learning (SSL) in DNA sequence classification, using FixMatch and FlexMatch with a GROVER DNA language model backbone. The authors find that augmentation designs tailored to biological constraints can yield more reliable gains than generic perturbations, though the abstract is truncated before reporting full results. The work provides practical guidance for choosing augmentation recipes in label-scarce genomic settings.

papers.title: Machine learning-derived intracellular protein-based prognostic model reflecting a senescence-associated secretory phenotype-driven immunosuppressive microenvironment in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the associations of senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-related genes with the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and clinical outcomes in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and to develop and evaluate a prognostic signature for risk stratification and exploratory treatment-response prediction.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to build a prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma based on intracellular protein levels linked to the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). The authors show that SASP-related gene signatures are associated with an immunosuppressive tumor immune microenvironment and with clinical outcomes, and they propose the model for risk stratification and exploratory prediction of treatment response.

papers.title: MRI-Based Radiomics Predicts FAP Expression and Immunosuppressive Tumor Microenvironment in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: To develop a Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) -based radiomics-clinical model for noninvasive prediction of fibroblast activation protein (FAP) expression in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and to explore its association with tumor microenvironment (TME) characteristics and potential immunotherapy response.
papers.summary: This study develops an MRI-based radiomics-clinical model to noninvasively predict fibroblast activation protein (FAP) expression in hepatocellular carcinoma, linking imaging features to an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. The work suggests radiomics could serve as a surrogate biomarker for FAP status and immunotherapy response, potentially guiding treatment decisions without biopsy.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence - driven toxicogenomics for predictive environmental and pharmaceutical safety.
papers.abstract: Toxicogenomics integrates high-throughput genomic technologies with toxicology to evaluate molecular responses to chemical and pharmaceutical exposures. The increasing volume and complexity of multi-omics data necessitate advanced computational approaches capable of extracting meaningful and predictive insights. In this context, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) techniques-including support vector machines, random forests, and deep learning architectures-are increasingly employed for early toxicity prediction and risk assessment, with reported improvements in predictive ac
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence and machine learning methods—such as support vector machines, random forests, and deep learning—are being applied to toxicogenomics data to predict the toxicity of environmental chemicals and pharmaceutical compounds. It argues that these computational approaches can extract predictive insights from complex multi-omics datasets, enabling earlier and more accurate safety risk assessment than traditional methods.

papers.title: Multi-source data integration and ensemble machine learning analysis of the role of Corilagin in regulating endoplasmic reticulum stress and alleviating intestinal ischemia reperfusion injury in mice.
papers.abstract: Intestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IIRI) is driven by oxidative stress, excessive inflammation, Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress (ERS), and disruption of the intestinal epithelial barrier. Corilagin, a natural ellagitannin with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, has shown protective effects against IIRI; however, its cross-species and multitarget mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-source data and ensemble machine learning to investigate how the natural compound Corilagin protects against intestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury in mice. The authors identify that Corilagin modulates endoplasmic reticulum stress pathways, reducing oxidative stress, inflammation, and epithelial barrier disruption. The work suggests cross-species and multi-target mechanisms underlying Corilagin's protective effects.

papers.title: Phenotyping of AMI patients using machine learning: integration of clinical, metabolic, and behavioral features to identify high-risk "frailty-inflammation" phenotype.
papers.abstract: Prognosis among patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) shows substantial heterogeneity, making precise identification of high-risk phenotypes essential for improving long-term outcomes. Machine learning techniques were used to identify such phenotypes by integrating multidimensional data and to examine their association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
papers.summary: This study applied machine learning to integrate clinical, metabolic, and behavioral data from acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients to identify distinct risk phenotypes. The analysis uncovered a high-risk "frailty-inflammation" phenotype that was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), suggesting that multidimensional phenotyping can improve risk stratification beyond traditional single-domain approaches.

papers.title: A comparative analysis of machine learning, deep learning, and ensemble learning models for suicidal ideation detection on social media.
papers.abstract: Suicidal ideation is the consideration of self-inflicted death and has emerged as a serious and rising concern for worldwide public health systems, contributing to over 800,000 deaths annually worldwide. Individuals express intentions, distress, and thoughts of self-harm and death, thereby offering a crucial and unprecedented avenue for timely psychological intervention and surveillance. The core problem addressed by this research is the pronounced global insufficiency in detecting and mitigating suicidal ideation across linguistically diverse environments, specifically focusing on low-resourc
papers.summary: This study compares machine learning, deep learning, and ensemble learning approaches for detecting suicidal ideation in social media text, with a focus on linguistically diverse, low-resource settings. The authors benchmark multiple model families to identify which performs best for this public-health surveillance task. The work is a comparative methodological evaluation rather than a new resource or biological finding.

papers.title: An Eight-Gene Metabolic Prognostic Signature in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Cross-Cohort Evaluation, Single-Cell Analysis, and Preliminary Functional Evaluation of PYGL and G6PD.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is the most prevalent pathological subtype of head and neck malignancies. Although metabolic reprogramming contributes to malignant progression and adaptation within the tumor microenvironment in HNSCC, its biological and prognostic implications remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study develops an eight-gene metabolic prognostic signature for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, validated across multiple cohorts and complemented by single-cell analysis. The authors also perform preliminary functional evaluation of two signature genes, PYGL and G6PD, linking metabolic reprogramming to tumor progression and patient outcome.

papers.title: Substrate secondary structure is associated with proteasomal cleavage propensity.
papers.abstract: Why does the proteasome cleave proteins at some peptide bonds but not others? Prior work has emphasized sequence motifs, amino acid properties, and proteasome isoform, but the role of local secondary-structure context remains unclear. Here, we evaluate whether helix, strand, and coil context help explain proteasomal cleavage and whether such information can improve cleavage-site prediction. By mining a human and viral PDB structure corpus, we found that high-confidence predicted cleavage sites are enriched in beta-strand extended conformations and depleted in coil-like regions. We then trained
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the local secondary structure of a protein substrate influences where the proteasome cleaves it. By mining human and viral structures from the PDB, the authors found that high-confidence predicted cleavage sites are enriched in beta-strand regions and depleted in coil-like regions. They then trained a model incorporating this structural context to improve cleavage-site prediction.

papers.title: Integrating transcriptomic analysis and experimental validation unravels autophagy- and lactylation-related gene signatures in acute myocardial infarction.
papers.abstract: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is a leading global health burden. While autophagy and lactylation are crucial in cardiovascular pathophysiology, their coordinated roles in AMI remain unclear. This study investigates the transcriptional signatures associated with both processes to identify diagnostic biomarkers.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic analysis with experimental validation to identify gene signatures related to both autophagy and lactylation in acute myocardial infarction (AMI). The authors propose candidate diagnostic biomarkers by examining coordinated transcriptional patterns of these two processes, which have individually been implicated in cardiovascular pathophysiology but not previously studied together in AMI.

papers.title: Development and internal validation of a predictive model for clinical deterioration in newly diagnosed lung cancer patients based on interpretable machine learning.
papers.abstract: To develop and validate an interpretable machine learning-based model for the early identification of the risk of clinical deterioration during hospitalization in newly diagnosed lung cancer patients.
papers.summary: This study develops and internally validates an interpretable machine-learning model to predict which newly diagnosed lung cancer patients will experience clinical deterioration during hospitalization. The work focuses on early risk identification using explainable ML techniques, though only internal validation is reported.

papers.title: Sequence-activity mapping and model-guided engineering of the phenol-responsive DmpR-Po σ54 promoter.
papers.abstract: Promoters are core cis-regulatory elements that determine gene expression levels and dynamic responses, and their quantitative engineering directly dictates the performance of synthetic biological systems such as whole-cell biosensors. However, the transcriptional output of complex inducible systems, exemplified by σ54-dependent promoters, relies on long-range coordination among distal bacterial enhancer-binding proteins, DNA architectural proteins, and RNA polymerase. The combined effects of multiple regulatory regions on promoter output remain poorly understood, which limits the cross-backgr
papers.summary: The authors systematically mapped how sequence variation across the regulatory regions of the phenol-responsive DmpR-Po σ54 promoter affects its transcriptional output, then used a model-guided approach to engineer improved promoter variants. This reveals how distal enhancer-binding sites, DNA architectural elements, and core promoter sequences jointly tune expression in a complex σ54-dependent inducible system. The resulting engineered promoters offer better-controlled, tunable components for whole-cell biosensors and other synthetic circuits.

papers.title: Evaluation of large language models for ICI-related liver injury with an emerging microbiome focus.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-related liver injury (ICI-LI) has heterogeneous phenotypes, a complex differential diagnosis, and evolving management. Gut microbiome research provides biological plausibility for immune regulation during ICI therapy, but evidence specific to ICI-LI remains limited and is not yet clinically actionable. We evaluated whether publicly accessible large language model (LLM) chatbots can organize this mixed evidence base and communicate its uncertainty.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether publicly accessible LLM chatbots can accurately organize and communicate the mixed, uncertain evidence base on immune checkpoint inhibitor-related liver injury (ICI-LI), including emerging gut microbiome findings. The work tests LLM performance in a clinical niche where evidence is heterogeneous and not yet actionable, focusing on how well models convey uncertainty rather than just factual recall.

papers.title: Natural language processing for suicidal behavior detection in short Spanish clinical notes from first-contact interviews.
papers.abstract: Suicide is a multifactorial phenomenon influenced by social, cultural, biological, and psychological factors, whose early detection remains challenging. According to the World Health Organization, suicide is the third leading cause of death among individuals aged 15-29 years, representing a major public health concern for young populations worldwide. In first-contact clinical settings, screening opportunities are often constrained by limited time, sparse patient information, and operational workflows. This study evaluates the feasibility of detecting suicidal behavior from short Spanish-langua
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether natural language processing can detect suicidal behavior from short Spanish-language clinical notes collected during first-contact interviews. The work addresses a challenging real-world setting where notes are brief and information is sparse, testing the feasibility of automated screening in time-constrained clinical workflows.

papers.title: Engineering a hemoglobin variant with enhanced stability and oxygen affinity using a protein language model.
papers.abstract: Engineered hemoglobin variants offer therapeutic promise for artificial blood substitutes and oxygen therapeutics, but rational design is constrained by protein stability and heme-binding. Protein language models (pLMs) predict mutation fitness, yet their integration with biophysical validation remains limited.
papers.summary: The authors use a protein language model to design hemoglobin variants with improved stability and oxygen affinity, then validate the top candidates experimentally. This demonstrates that pLM-guided mutation prediction can be combined with biophysical assays to engineer oxygen-carrying proteins, a step toward artificial blood substitutes.

papers.title: AIPFusion-Net: an interaction-fusion framework for anti-inflammatory peptide prediction using protein language model embeddings, local sequence patterns, and handcrafted descriptors.
papers.abstract: Anti-inflammatory peptides (AIPs) are promising candidates for treating inflammatory diseases. However, experimental identification is time-consuming and costly, creating a need for accurate computational prediction methods.
papers.summary: The paper introduces AIPFusion-Net, a computational framework for predicting anti-inflammatory peptides by combining protein language model embeddings, local sequence patterns, and handcrafted descriptors in an interaction-fusion architecture. This addresses the high cost and time required for experimental identification of AIPs, offering a potentially accurate in silico screening tool for inflammatory disease therapeutics.

papers.title: Characterization and clustering of immunocompetent proteins based on ESM-2 sequence embedding and physicochemical feature fusion.
papers.abstract: Traditional sequence-comparison methods face challenges when classifying and identifying low-homology proteins formed by convergent evolution. In this exploratory study, we built a PCA-based unsupervised clustering workflow combining high-dimensional embeddings from the frozen pre-trained protein-language model ESM-2 and weighted-fused physicochemical features. The workflow was explored for family-level grouping, identification of putative functional conservation, and cross-species evolutionary analysis of immune-active proteins. An independent external test dataset was further used to prelimi
papers.summary: This exploratory study combines ESM-2 protein language model embeddings with physicochemical features in a PCA-based unsupervised clustering workflow to classify immunocompetent proteins, including low-homology proteins that traditional sequence comparison struggles with. The approach was tested for family-level grouping, functional conservation detection, and cross-species evolutionary analysis, with preliminary validation on an external dataset. It suggests that fusing learned embeddings with biophysical descriptors can aid protein classification where sequence homology is weak.

papers.title: Integrated computation-guided thermostabilization of the fungal sweet protein Honey Truffle Sweetener.
papers.abstract: Thermostability limits the use of sweet proteins as sugar substitutes in thermally processed foods. Here, we report an integrated computation-guided workflow for thermostabilizing Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS), a recently identified fungal sweet protein with low intrinsic stability. We determined the HTS crystal structure and used it to guide subsequent computational analyses. Rosetta and ThermoMPNN evaluated candidate substitutions from complementary physics-based and deep-learning-based perspectives, and the selected single-mutant library was experimentally characterized. The resulting melti
papers.summary: The authors determined the crystal structure of Honey Truffle Sweetener, a fungal sweet protein with poor heat stability, and used it to guide computational design of stabilizing mutations. Combining physics-based (Rosetta) and deep-learning (ThermoMPNN) predictions, they built and experimentally tested a single-mutant library, yielding variants with improved melting temperatures. This provides a general workflow for thermostabilizing food-relevant proteins.
